required_leakage_and_integrity_tests.required: Label maturity: for every fold and every target, every training event's target labels are available before the fold's first test cutoff (the harness asserts the block-boundary slack).
Injected future: changing the labels of any later event changes no earlier prediction.
History features: an event's issuer_history_rate uses only training-block events whose labels were available at its cutoff; none uses a test-block label.
Holdout sealing: no code path reads a block-5 outcome except the single look, and every read is logged.
Protocol integrity: every run first recomputes this file's canonical sha256 and the pinned input hashes, and refuses to run on any mismatch.
Determinism: the same inputs and seeds give identical canonical outputs and hashes.
Clusters: no reaction session or block is split between training and test.
Abstention: INSUFFICIENT_DATA and MODEL_FIT_FAILED produce null predictions with reasons, never substitutes.

from_the_protocol: A convenience sample of 23 issuers, conditioned on survival to 2026 and on reviewability; not a market sample, and no base rate here is a market base rate
SIC codes read on 2026-09-26, not as of the event dates
Time and selection regime are confounded in block 5
Events share 73 reaction sessions and come from 23 issuers; intervals are cluster-aware but remain approximate at these sizes
One market regime in the span; no execution data
Rare large moves (gaps of 15% and more) are out of reach of this dataset; it contains earnings releases only
limits.holdout_selection_regime: Block 5 is entirely Milestone 1 events, which were selected very differently from the rest (23 of 243 candidates kept, against 91% to 94% for steps 2 and 3). Time and selection regime are confounded in it; every holdout result carries that statement.
limits.what_the_holdout_is_for: a replication check on direction and a single, logged exposure of the frozen pipeline to data it was not developed on; not a source of statistical power
limits.not_blind_to_counts: Descriptive counts of block-5 outcomes, including positives per target, were already visible in the scoping evidence before this protocol was frozen. The holdout is sealed against model selection and tuning, not against knowledge of its base rates.
cannot_establish: stability across market regimes (one regime in the span)
performance after execution costs (no execution data)
known_consequences_stated_in_advance: In the clean-window version, loses_half_of_gap has 9 training positives in development fold 3 (threshold 10): that fold is INSUFFICIENT_DATA for it, its pooled development test set is then fold 4 alone (10 events), and so loses_half_of_gap is INSUFFICIENT_DATA for the clean-window claim rule. Its all-event results are still reported, as exploratory.
gap_ge_5pct has exactly 10 positives in the pooled development test set in both versions, the minimum that passes.
In the holdout, gap_ge_3pct, gap_ge_5pct and loses_half_of_gap have 3 to 5 positives in both versions and so are COUNTS_ONLY; extension_after_open_ge_5pct and day1_close_return meet their thresholds.
With 43 or 44 pooled test events and a 99% interval, a DISTINGUISHABLE_BETTER status needs a very large improvement over the base rate; most primaries are expected to be NOT_DISTINGUISHABLE.
limits.expected_outcome_stated_in_advance: For most targets the result is expected to be NOT_DISTINGUISHABLE from the pooled base rate, and the final holdout is expected to support counts only for most targets. Both are acceptable, reportable outcomes of this protocol.
limits.the_intervals_cover: uncertainty from the finite test sample and its clustering; it does not cover variability of the fitted models across training sets

open_for_the_owner.status: The owner has not answered these. The defaults are in force, protocol version 1 is unchanged, and changing any of them now would be a new protocol version stated to follow results of the earlier phases.
from_the_protocol_to_review: Whether the two thin primaries (gap_ge_5pct with 29 positives, loses_half_of_gap with 25) belong among the primaries
The 99% claim level, which makes any claim very hard at these sample sizes
That the holdout will mostly be counts-only
The issuer-history and sector features, given the point-in-time limits and small cells
protocol_silent_details_that_could_move_: the headline interval is the wider of the two by width (reaction_session on a tie)
regression history mean with no earlier event: ProtocolGap, no default
standardization: population or sample standard deviation (not implemented yet)
a predictor that fails in one fold takes that state for its whole pooled result
the group prior obeys the same maturity and earlier-session rules as the issuer's own history
protocol_silent_details_presentational_o: seeds and random draws per context
40 training events counted with the target defined
unnamed sector divisions are a ProtocolGap
a pooled test below its thresholds makes no predictions

replay_tests.decided: The replays that re-read the block-5 outcomes to verify the look are counted as accesses (the owner's decision of 2026-10-07T19:14:34.716Z: "Count the replays as accesses.").

opt_in.meaning: ReplayTests (tests/test_m4_phase4_results.py) are skipped unless the environment variable M4_REPLAY_HOLDOUT is exactly 1, so routine runs of the suite and CI no longer read the sealed block-5 outcomes. A run made on purpose is still two counted accesses and is added to this record when it is made.

acceptance_criteria.meaning: The report is acceptable when: this protocol was frozen before evaluation; the integrity tests above pass; every output reproduces deterministically from committed inputs; every target is reported with counts and cluster-aware intervals or as INSUFFICIENT_DATA; every predictor is compared with the pooled comparator C1 and, for binary targets, the seeded random ranking, clean-window and all-event side by side; calibration is shown with coarse bins and their counts; the holdout was looked at once; and the limits are stated. The acceptance decision is the owner's.
acceptance_criteria.does_not_require: that any predictor beats the base rate

not_a_claim: Not a claim of a predictive edge: no status in the protocol, including DISTINGUISHABLE_BETTER, is one.
Not evidence about any market: a convenience sample of 23 issuers on one regime, and block 5 is entirely Milestone 1 events (time and selection regime are confounded).
Not Milestone 4 acceptance: the protocol makes that decision the owner's, and nothing here makes it.
